Application Materials.content:
- Referees must submit their forms of reference via the hyperlink provided in the email invitation with the subject “Request for Statement of Reference” before the upcoming application deadline. **At least one of them must be an academic referee from the university that you have graduated or will graduate from.** The academic referee(s) is required to provide an official profile or directory link from the university website when completing the form of reference; forms without this profile or directory link will be considered incomplete, and the application will NOT be further processed.
- Upload the following supporting documents to the HKU Business School TPG Application Document Upload System **no later than TWO working days after the application deadline** of the round you are applying to. If there are further updates, upload a full set of the updated documents under that category; the new submission will overwrite the previous submission.
- CV.
- Academic Certificate: graduate transcript/latest official transcript; Graduation Certificate/Online Verification Report of Higher Education Qualification Certificate, applicable to candidates from Mainland China institutions only; Bachelor’s degree certificate/Online Verification Report of Higher Education Degree Certificate, applicable to candidates from Mainland China institutions only; official ranking certificate, **in ONE single PDF file**. Documents not in English should be accompanied by a formally certified English translation. Both Chinese and English versions are required for the online verification reports, and the validity period should be set to 6 months or the longest available.
- Working Experience Proof: valid employment proof of internship of all positions, or most recent full-time employment, whichever is applicable. Contract/correspondences with working colleagues are not accepted as employment proof. Submit **in ONE single PDF file**.
- Language Report, **in ONE single PDF file**.
- Photo Identification: Passport page with photo / ID Card / Exit-Entry Permit, etc., **in ONE single PDF file**.
- Others: Personal statement; GMAT/GRE score report; Certificates of Professional qualifications e.g. ACCA, CFA, CPA; etc., **in ONE single PDF file**.
- You may be invited to record and upload admission videos as additional mandatory supporting documents. Applications with missing supporting documents will be considered incomplete and will NOT be processed further.
- In the application stage, the original copy of supporting documents is NOT required; candidates only need to upload the softcopy to the HKU Business School TPG Application Document Upload System. If an admission offer is received, original/certified true copies of the documents will be required.

Interview Requirements.content: In general, applicants are not required to attend an interview during the admissions process. You may be invited to record and upload additional mandatory admission videos.

Application Deadlines.content: Application rounds for **2027 intake** are now open. Supporting documents must be uploaded no later than **TWO working days** after the application deadline of the round you are applying to.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: *Candidates with a good GMAT/GRE score will be favorably considered.* Should candidates wish to submit a GMAT or GRE score, they should upload a copy of the test report together with other supporting documents to the application system. The GMAT code for HKU Master of Accounting Analytics programme is **FS2-WL-97**. The HKU GRE code is **2482**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Candidates who wish to be admitted on the basis of a qualification from a university or comparable institution outside Hong Kong where the language of teaching and/or examination is not English are required to obtain **a score of 80 in the internet-based TOEFL**. **A minimum overall band of 6 with no subtest lower than 5.5 in IELTS** is also accepted. In exceptional circumstances they may be exempted from this requirement.
IELTS and TOEFL tests must be taken within **two years prior to September 1 of each admissions year**. Test scores more than two years are not accepted. **TOEFL iBT Home Edition and IELTS One Skill Retake will not be accepted**. When candidates pre-register to take the test, they should request that the official test scores be sent to The University of Hong Kong. The **HKU TOEFL code number is 9671**.

Program Overview.content:
The Master of Accounting Analytics programme offered by the HKU Business School aims to develop accounting professionals equipped with data analytics skills and is specifically designed to foster talents capable of transforming raw and intricate accounting data into actionable intelligence for addressing general accounting-related questions. The primary focus of the programme is to equip students with specialised tools used in the accounting industry to cope with the increasing market demand.
The programme trains accounting professionals with both technical and accounting expertise through the utilisation of data, information technology, statistical analysis, quantitative methods, and mathematical or computer-based models, as well as foundational accounting courses to meet the requirement of professional bodies. Incoming students with diverse undergraduate backgrounds are attracted, and experiences in accounting and/or technology can be highly valuable.
Graduates can anticipate a wide array of analytics-related career opportunities across various levels, from junior to senior positions, in both private and public sectors. These opportunities encompass data-driven decision making, cost control, fraud detection and prevention, performance evaluation, forecasting and budgeting, compliance, and risk management. Graduates will be well-positioned to explore careers in industries that increasingly rely on data analytics.
The programme includes pre-programme boot camp, core courses, elective courses, and a capstone course. The capstone course allows students to integrate and apply knowledge and techniques learned in previous courses in a business project using real-world data, including project planning and management, strategy setting, model building, data analysis and interpretation, and result presentation.
Our Faculty includes [Prof. Anson Yile JIANG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/anson-yile-jiang/), [Prof. Wei LUO](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/wei-luo-2/), [Dr. Kin Hang CHAN](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/kin-hang-chan), [Prof. Michael CHAU](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/michael-c-l-chau/), [Prof. Hailiang CHEN](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/hailiang-chen/), [Prof. Travis CHOW](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/travis-chow/), [Prof. Pingyang GAO](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/pingyang-gao), [Prof. Keri HU](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/keri-peicong-hu/), [Dr. Jasmine KWONG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/jasmine-kwong/), [Prof. David LEE](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/david-s-lee/), [Prof. Xiao LEI](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/xiao-lei/), [Prof. Winnie LEUNG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/winnie-s-c-leung/), [Prof. Peeyush TAORI](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/peeyush-taori/), [Prof. Xin WANG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/xin-wang/), [Prof. Yan XIONG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/yan-xiong/) Ph.D., University of Toronto, MAA Programme Director, Prof. Joseph XU Ph.D, University of Pennsylvania; Chief Technology Officer, Chainproof Digital Asset Insurance Ltd., [Prof. Sammy FUNG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/sammy-fung/), [Prof. Simon S.K. The programme is accredited by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), CPA Australia, Chartered Global Management Accountants (CGMA), and the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA).

Curriculum.content:
The Master of Accounting Analytics curriculum includes mandatory pre-programme boot camp courses, core courses, elective courses, and a capstone course.
- Mandatory boot camp courses cover: Economics; Preparatory Course for Accounting Fundamentals; Introduction to Python and Vibe Coding for Accounting Analytics. Each topic consists of 15 hours of interactive lectures and, for Economics, an examination at the end. Students are required to attend all classes and pass all boot camp courses.
- Refresher course on fundamental accounting concepts, Preparatory Course for Accounting Fundamentals, will also be provided to brush up students' accounting skills.
- Course exemption of up to two required courses, except the capstone course, may be granted normally by examination if candidates can produce evidence that a course is equivalent in content to another course taken elsewhere with a satisfactory grade, or are holding relevant professional qualifications obtained before admission to the curriculum. No credits will be given for the exempted course and candidates shall be required to take an approved alternative course of the same credit value.
Core courses listed include:
- PMAA7005 Integrated Auditing: Bridging the Gap Between IT Audit and Financial Statement Audit
- PMAA7004 Advanced Accounting Analytics
- PMAA7003 Accounting Analytics Foundation
- PMAA7002 Data Modelling and Economic Decisions
- PMAA7001 Accounting and Business Intelligence
Elective courses listed include:
- PMAA7008 Blockchain, Cryptocurrency and Cybersecurity
- PMAA7009 Accounting, Fintech and Innovation
- PMAA7010 Data Mining and Text Analysis
- PMAA7011 Deep Learning and Neural Networks
- PMAA7012 Taxation Framework and Planning
- PMAA7013 Corporate Finance
- PMAA7014 Principles of Management
- PMAA7015 ESG Reporting: Concepts and Practices
- PMAA7016 Accounting Analytics and Managerial Decisions
- PMAA7017 Social Media and Digital Marketing Analytics
- PMAA7018 Database Design and Management
- PMAA7019 Advanced Financial Reporting: A Case-Based Approach
- PMAA7020 Legal and Ethical Environment of Business
- PMAA7021 International Study Field Trip
- PMAA7022 Fundamentals of Banking Institutions
- PMAA7024 Financial Statement Analysis: A Data Analytic Approach
- PMAA7025 AI for Financial Valuation and Investment
Other Masters Programmes electives: Candidates may take up to two elective courses from other taught postgraduate curricula offered by the Faculty of Business and Economics under the advice and approval of the Programme Directors concerned. Students can take up to two electives from the Master of Accounting, Master of Artificial Intelligence in Business, Master of Economics, Master of Finance, Master of Global Management, Master of Science in Business Analytics, Master of Science in Marketing, Master of Sustainable Accounting and Finance or Master of Wealth Management programme at HKU. Enrollment in electives from other programmes is subject to seat availability and approval by the Programme Directors concerned based on the student's profile, capabilities and performance in the MAA programme. Since enrollment in other taught postgraduate electives is not guaranteed, students should always choose two MAA electives during course enrollment.
Capstone Course (Choose One):
- PMAA7007 Artificial Intelligence in Accounting
- PMSC7901 Business Case Analysis Capstone

Other expenses to consider when renting outside campus include agent commission, typically **50% of one month's rent**; deposit, usually **2 months' rent**; stamp duty, where for a $10,000/month rental, the tenant pays around **$300**; and miscellaneous moving-in costs like furniture and household items.
Meal expenses: on campus, students would expect spending an average of **HK$25 - HK$65 per meal**, depending on the time of the day and personal food preference. Transportation cost reference fares include Sassoon Road to Main Campus **HK$2-7** by University shuttle bus or **HK$5.1-14.5** by bus or minibus; Main Campus to Central **HK$5.9-9.4** by bus or MTR; and Main Campus to Causeway Bay/Mongkok **HK$5.9-20** by bus, minibus or MTR.
For non-local students, on top of tuition fees, expenses for the first month can amount to **HK$10,000 or more** for a student, including rental charges, household items and textbooks.

Financial Aid.content:
In 2024, the Faculty of Business and Economics established the Master of Accounting Analytics Scholarship for students of the Master of Accounting Analytics (MAA) programme.
The Scholarship shall be awarded annually either as an Entrance Scholarship to new full-time MAA students or a Merit-based Scholarship to current full-time MAA students.
For the Entrance Scholarship, the number of scholarships to be awarded each year and the value of each scholarship shall be determined by the Faculty Scholarship Committee, upon funding availability and recommendation of the MAA Admissions Committee based on the following criteria:
1. Reputation of candidates’ previous undergraduate or postgraduate institution;
2. Academic performance;
3. Prior international experience; and
4. Relevance of full-time work experience after the first degree.
Financial need may also be taken into consideration. The Scholarship shall not be paid directly to the awardees, but rather be applied to cover their composition fees. In exceptional case, for students who are granted with full scholarship, an additional amount might be granted in the form of subsistence allowance. In any event, the value of each scholarship shall not be less than **HK$10,000**.
For the Merit-based Scholarship, the number of awards shall not exceed **20% of the class size** in the relevant academic year, and the value of each scholarship shall be **10% of the composition fee** of the given intake. The exact number of scholarships shall be determined by the Faculty Scholarship Committee, upon funding availability and recommendation of the MAA Programme Director based on the following criteria:
1. Academic performance in first three modules of the relevant academic year;
2. Participation in extracurricular activities arranged by the programme office and the career and enrichment teams, including, but not limited to, industry seminars, career workshops and student activities, in the first three modules of the relevant academic year;
3. Recommendations from the course instructors of the first three modules in the relevant academic year on the course performance and class participation; and,
4. Level of support provided to the programme office in marketing and admissions efforts, student activities and other programme-related initiatives.

Multiple Applications.content: Yes, it is possible for you to apply to multiple programmes at HKU. You can apply under different usernames on the application system and pay the application fee (**HK$600**) for each programme that you wish to apply to. You can only enrol in one programme, even if you receive offers from other programmes.

Conditional Admission Policy.content: Students may apply for entry for study with a Conditional Admission Offer. **Upon receipt of the Firm Admission Offer, students are required to upload the copy of the Firm Offer to the HKU Student Visa Application System.** Otherwise, Admissions Office will not issue the approved visa/entry permit. Students are strongly advised to start the application before the deadline in order to obtain the student visa before the start of the semester.
